questions.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “capital” most nearly mean?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The columns were roughed out in the quarry and finished on site. Each <u>capital</u> was cut last of all, partly because its acanthus leaves were the part most easily chipped in transport and partly because the carver wanted to see the shaft standing in place before deciding how deeply to undercut the stone.

choices.label: A

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A skyscraper does not resist the wind by rigidity alone. Near the top of Taipei 101 hangs a polished steel sphere weighing 660 tonnes, suspended on cables and free to swing. When the tower leans in a gust the sphere lags behind and pulls against the motion. <u>Sway on the upper floors is cut by roughly forty per cent, which is the difference between a nuisance and an evacuation.</u>

choices.label: A
choices.content: It introduces a second engineering problem that the text goes on to solve.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It questions whether the sphere performs as its designers intended.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It explains the method by which the sphere is suspended.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It quantifies the effect of the device just described and indicates why that effect matters.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Ainu weavers make attush cloth from the inner bark of the elm. <u>The bark has to be stripped in early summer, while the sap is running, or it cannot be separated into usable fibre at all.</u> Once the strips have been soaked in a stream and split by hand, they are spun and woven on a body-tension loom, then dyed in patterns that also appear on Ainu woodcarving.

choices.label: A
choices.content: It argues that elm bark is superior to other fibres used in weaving.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It explains why attush patterns resemble the patterns on Ainu woodcarving.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It contrasts two competing methods of preparing bark for the loom.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It identifies a constraint that governs when the raw material can be gathered.

questions.stem: According to the text, why is radiolarian ooze useful to geologists?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Radiolarians are single-celled drifters that build intricate skeletons out of silica. When they die the skeletons sink, and over millions of years they pile up on the deep seafloor as a fine ooze. Because different radiolarian species lived in different intervals, and because the shape of a skeleton reflects the water the animal grew in, a core drilled through the ooze gives geologists both a calendar and a thermometer for ancient oceans.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Silica skeletons can be dated more easily than carbonate ones.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It contains the only fossils that survive at great depth in the ocean.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Species turnover within it marks time while skeleton shape indicates past conditions.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It accumulates quickly enough to record events from one year to the next.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Nüshu, a script used by women in one corner of Hunan, was written on folding fans and embroidered handkerchiefs rather than on paper. Its characters are not the characters that boys learned in school; they are slanted, thinner in the stroke, and they record the local speech by sound rather than by meaning. Women who had never been taught to read the official script could nevertheless read one another.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Nüshu gave women a means of writing to each other independent of the official script.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Nüshu was written on cloth because paper was scarce in that part of Hunan.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Men in Hunan were forbidden from learning to read Nüshu.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Nüshu was a decorative variant of the characters taught in Hunan schools.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Solheim's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The Norse settlements in Greenland were abandoned during the fifteenth century. Historian Petra Solheim argues that the cause was economic: walrus ivory, effectively the colony's only export, lost its European market once elephant ivory became available again. Others point instead to a cooling climate that shortened the growing season for the colony's hay.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Norse farmers in Iceland came through the same period without abandoning their farms.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Ice cores show that summers in southern Greenland grew colder from about 1350 onward.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Hay yields recorded at the settlements were normal in the years before abandonment, and the collapse in ivory prices preceded the departures.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The walrus hunting grounds lay several weeks' sail north of the settlements.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Novak's explanation over the alternative?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Great tits living in cities sing at a higher pitch than those in woodland a few kilometres away. Ornithologist Karel Novak argues that the shift is a response to low-frequency traffic noise, which would otherwise mask their songs. Others suggest that city birds are simply smaller on average, and that smaller birds sing higher.

choices.label: A
choices.content: City great tits weigh slightly less on average than woodland great tits.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Individual birds raise the pitch of their song within minutes when nearby traffic noise increases.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Traffic noise in the cities studied is concentrated below two kilohertz.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Great tits in cities defend smaller territories than those in woodland.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly undermine the conservator's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Large bronzes were usually cast in pieces and joined afterwards, since a single pour of that volume is difficult to control. A conservator argues that one particular figure was instead cast in a single pour, citing the complete absence of visible joins anywhere on its surface.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The alloy composition of the figure is uniform throughout.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Casting a figure of this size in one pour was technically possible at the time it was made.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The figure stands on a base that was cast separately from the body.

choices.label: D
choices.content: X-rays of comparable figures show that joins between separately cast parts were routinely filed down and disguised.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

questions.passage: Moths caught at street lights were found to fly in tighter spirals than moths netted in unlit fields a kilometre away. The researchers are careful to note that they sampled only moths already gathered at the lights. If the moths that spiral tightly are also the ones drawn to lights in the first place, then the finding _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: would be reversed if the lights were switched off for a whole season.

choices.label: B
choices.content: applies only to the unlit fields that were sampled.

choices.label: C
choices.content: shows that artificial light alters the flight of moths over time.

choices.label: D
choices.content: may reflect which moths are drawn to lights rather than any effect of the light on flight.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

Linear A uses many of the same signs, but applying the Linear B sound values to it yields no words in any language anyone has been able to identify. choices.label: B

questions.stem: The student wants to explain what the new sewers changed and what followed from the change. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The Thames was so foul in the summer of 1858 that Parliament hung lime-soaked curtains at its windows.
  • Joseph Bazalgette was authorised that year to build a system of intercepting sewers.
  • The sewers carried waste to outfalls downstream of the city instead of into the central Thames.
  • Cholera deaths in the districts they served fell sharply afterwards.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Parliament hung lime-soaked curtains at its windows during the summer of 1858.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The intercepting sewers carried waste to outfalls downstream of the city rather than into the central Thames, and cholera deaths in the districts they served fell sharply.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Joseph Bazalgette was authorised in 1858 to build a system of intercepting sewers.

choices.label: D

questions.stem: The student wants to emphasise that the record was designed to be understood by a finder who shares no language with its makers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

questions.passage:

choices.label: A
choices.content: The Voyager probes each carry a gold-plated copper disc fixed to them before launch in 1977.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Since any finder would share no language with the record's makers, the instructions for playing it are etched on the cover as diagrams.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The record carries spoken greetings in 55 languages along with music and images.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Both Voyager probes have now passed beyond the heliosphere.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain how a fog net produces water. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Fog nets are panels of fine mesh strung across ridges on the Chilean coast.
  • Fog blown against the mesh condenses on the threads and runs down into a gutter.
  • One large net can yield several hundred litres on a foggy day.
  • A village in the region has used the nets to supply a small brewery.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Several hundred litres of water can be collected from a single net on a foggy day.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Fog nets are panels of fine mesh strung across ridges on the Chilean coast.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Fog blown against the mesh condenses on the threads and runs down into a gutter, so that one large net yields several hundred litres on a foggy day.

choices.label: D
choices.content: A village on the Chilean coast has used fog nets to supply a small brewery.

choices.label: D

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A kgotla is a Tswana assembly held in the open, usually in the shade of a particular tree. He listens, and at the end he states the sense of the meeting; a chief who states it wrongly can expect to be corrected on the spot.

choices.content: It presents a chronological account of how the kgotla developed.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It raises a criticism of the kgotla and then rebuts that criticism.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It defines an institution, describes how its proceedings run, and specifies the limited role of its leader.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It compares two forms of assembly and argues that one of them is fairer.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Writing in Mesopotamia did not begin with poetry. The earliest tablets record quantities of barley, beer and livestock, and their signs descend from small clay tokens once sealed inside hollow clay envelopes to certify a debt. To show what an envelope held, the tokens were pressed into its outer surface before it was closed. Someone eventually noticed that the impressions made the tokens inside unnecessary.

choices.label: A
choices.content: To explain the administrative origins of a writing system.

choices.label: B
choices.content: To argue that Mesopotamian literature has been undervalued.

choices.label: C
choices.content: To describe how clay tablets were fired and then stored.

choices.label: D

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The warship Vasa capsized in Stockholm harbour in 1628, less than a mile from where she was launched. She lay in the mud for 333 years and came up with her carvings still crisp. The Baltic is too brackish for the shipworm that would have eaten an oak hull in open salt water, and the harbour mud sealed her timbers away from oxygen. What sank the ship is also what saved her.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Shipworms are the principal threat to wooden wrecks in all waters.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Stockholm harbour has preserved a number of seventeenth-century vessels.

choices.label: C

questions.stem: According to the text, why did perfumers prize aged ambergris?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Ambergris forms in the gut of a sperm whale around the indigestible beaks of the squid it swallows. choices.label: B
choices.content: Because it was the strongest-smelling material available to them.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Because it made other scents last longer rather than for its own odour.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Because it could be gathered fresh from beaches in large quantities.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Duarte's claim?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Two bells cast from the same bronze can sound quite unlike each other. choices.label: A
choices.content: Bells cast to the same profile from alloys of differing tin content sound nearly identical.

choices.content: Bells with a higher tin content are harder and more brittle than bells with less.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Kaur's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Membership of Britain's friendly societies, which pooled workers' contributions to pay sickness benefits, fell sharply after 1911. Sociologist Denis Kaur argues that the state insurance scheme introduced in that year displaced them. choices.label: A
choices.content: The state scheme paid a smaller weekly benefit than most societies did.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Urban branches of the societies had always been smaller than rural ones.

choices.label: C
choices.content: In districts where movement into the cities was negligible, membership fell just as steeply after 1911.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Friendly societies had been losing members slowly since the 1890s.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Adeli's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A qanat is a gently sloping tunnel that carries groundwater from a mountain aquifer to a village, and it silts up unless it is cleaned every few years. Historian Farah Adeli argues that the qanats of one Iranian valley stayed in use for eight centuries because of a customary law assigning each household a share of the maintenance in proportion to its share of the water, and not merely because the geology there was favourable.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Neighbouring valleys with the same geology, but without such a customary law, saw their qanats abandoned within two centuries.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The valley's aquifer is recharged by snowmelt every spring.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The qanat tunnels in the valley are lined throughout with fired clay hoops.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The customary law was first written down in the nineteenth century.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

The herbarium's collection of ferns, together with its several thousand lichen specimens, _____ digitised over the winter, sheet by sheet.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The eruption of Mount Tambora in 1815 was the largest anywhere in the past thousand years, and it threw enough ash and sulphur into the stratosphere to dim sunlight across the whole of the northern hemisphere. _____ farmers in New England recorded frost in every month of the following summer.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

questions.passage: Resurrection plants can lose almost all the water in their tissues and lie dormant for years, greening again within hours of a rain. _____ brine shrimp lay eggs that survive being dried out completely and hatch when a desert pool refills.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why the 1769 expeditions had to be sent so far apart. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • In 1769 observers were sent to Tahiti, to Hudson Bay and to Lapland.
  • Each timed the passage of Venus across the face of the Sun.
  • The Sun's distance is calculated by comparing timings taken from widely separated places.
  • Transits of Venus come in pairs eight years apart and then not again for over a century.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Because the Sun's distance is calculated by comparing timings from widely separated places, observers were sent as far apart as Tahiti and Lapland.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Transits of Venus come in pairs eight years apart and then not again for more than a century.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Each observer timed the passage of Venus across the face of the Sun.

choices.label: D
choices.content: In 1769 observers travelled to Tahiti, to Hudson Bay and to Lapland to watch the transit.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why the replica was built. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The painted cave at Lascaux was opened to visitors in 1948.
  • Carbon dioxide and moisture from visitors' breath encouraged algae and crystal growth on the painted surfaces.
  • The cave was closed to the public in 1963.
  • A full-size replica opened a short distance away in 1983.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Lascaux was open to visitors for fifteen years, between 1948 and 1963.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Algae and crystals grew over the painted surfaces inside the cave.

choices.label: C
choices.content: A full-size replica of the painted cave opened a short distance from Lascaux in 1983.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Because moisture and carbon dioxide from visitors' breath were damaging the paintings, the cave was closed in 1963 and a full-size replica opened nearby in 1983.

questions.stem: The student wants to convey how effective the approach has proved. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Conventional paving sheds rainfall straight into storm drains.
  • Sponge city designs use permeable paving, constructed wetlands and rooftop planting.
  • These surfaces absorb rain where it falls and release it slowly.
  • Trial districts in Wuhan cut peak storm runoff by about half.

choices.label: A
choices.content: By absorbing rain where it falls, trial districts in Wuhan cut peak storm runoff by about half.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Conventional paving sheds rainfall straight into the storm drains.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Sponge city designs use permeable paving, constructed wetlands and rooftop planting.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Permeable surfaces absorb rain where it falls and then release it slowly.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The Nabataeans built Petra in a desert that receives less than fifteen centimetres of rain in a year. Channels cut into the sandstone caught whatever fell on the surrounding slopes and carried it to cisterns hollowed out beneath the streets, so that the city's water supply stayed _____ even through years in which no rain fell at all.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Inca administrators kept their records on quipus, bundles of cords in which the type of knot and its position along the cord both carried meaning. Spanish officials who could not read them assumed the cords were ornamental. Modern study has shown the opposite: the quipu is a _____ system, capable of holding censuses, tribute rolls and dates with precision.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The retroreflectors left on the lunar surface by Apollo crews send a laser pulse straight back to whichever telescope fired it. Timing the round trip gives the Earth-Moon distance to within a few centimetres, and repeating that measurement for half a century has shown the Moon to be _____ from the Earth by about 3.8 centimetres a year.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Byssus is the fine thread a pen shell spins to anchor itself to the seabed. Gathered and combed, it was once woven into gloves light enough to be folded inside a walnut shell. Few weavers ever learned the technique, and today it is practised by a single family on Sardinia; the craft is thus all but _____.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Making katsuobushi takes the better part of a year. The fish is simmered, then smoked over many separate firings, then deliberately inoculated with a mould that draws out the last of the moisture. The finished block is hard enough that it must be shaved with a plane, and the process is far too _____ to be hurried along by machinery.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Dating a violin used to mean trusting the label pasted inside it. Now a good photograph of the spruce top will often do: the growth rings visible in the wood can be matched against master chronologies assembled from thousands of Alpine trees. <u>An instrument cannot have been made before its youngest ring finished growing.</u> Several violins bearing eighteenth-century labels have turned out to contain wood felled a full century later.

choices.label: A
choices.content: It offers an example of an instrument found to be mislabelled.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It states the principle that makes the dating method decisive.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It concedes a weakness in the ring-matching technique.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It describes how the master chronologies are assembled.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: For three decades in the nineteenth century the Chincha Islands off Peru supplied Europe with the most effective fertiliser then obtainable: seabird guano, laid down over millennia on rock that almost never sees rain. Ships waited months in the roadstead for a cargo, and two governments went to war over the trade. Then the deposits ran out. Nitrate mines and later synthetic ammonia took the market, and the islands are now visited mainly by ornithologists.

choices.label: A
choices.content: To trace the rise and collapse of a trade and note what became of its source.

choices.label: B
choices.content: To argue that synthetic ammonia was a more sustainable alternative to guano.

choices.label: C
choices.content: To describe the working conditions of the labourers on the Chincha Islands.

choices.label: D
choices.content: To explain the chemical properties that made guano so effective as a fertiliser.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Leafcutter ants do not eat the leaves they carry into the nest. They chew them into a mulch, and on that mulch they grow a fungus, and the fungus is what feeds the colony. The garden is vulnerable to a parasitic mould that would overrun it in days. On their bodies the ants carry a bacterium producing a compound that suppresses exactly that mould; remove the bacterium and the garden fails.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Leafcutter ants feed on leaves that they first soften into a mulch.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The colony depends on a cultivated fungus, which a bacterium carried by the ants protects.

choices.label: C
choices.content: A parasitic mould has caused the collapse of many leafcutter colonies.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The bacterium carried by the ants is the colony's principal source of food.

questions.stem: According to the text, what is the vault's function?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The seed vault on Svalbard is cut into a mountainside above the permafrost line. Its purpose is not to collect seed in its own right but to hold duplicates of collections kept elsewhere, so that a gene bank destroyed by war, fire or accident can be restocked from the copies. Depositors keep ownership of their own boxes, and the vault has been drawn on only once, at the request of a collection displaced from Syria.

choices.label: A
choices.content: To gather wild plant species that no other gene bank holds.

choices.label: B
choices.content: To keep backup copies for gene banks that may lose their own holdings.

choices.label: C
choices.content: To distribute seed to farmers in the aftermath of natural disasters.

choices.label: D
choices.content: To hold seed whose ownership its depositors have signed over to Norway.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Waititi's argument over the rival one?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The sweet potato is native to South America, yet it was being grown across Polynesia well before any European ship reached the Pacific. Botanist Hine Waititi argues that Polynesian voyagers reached the American coast and carried the plant home with them. A rival account holds that seed capsules drifted across the ocean unaided and took root where they washed ashore.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Sweet potatoes grow well in the soils of several Pacific island groups.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Coastal peoples in South America cultivated a number of distinct sweet potato varieties.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Sweet potato seed capsules can remain viable in seawater for several weeks.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The Polynesian name for the plant closely resembles the name used for it on the South American coast.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Oyelaran's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Many pterosaurs carried a bony crest on the skull, and in some species it projected backwards further than the length of the skull itself. Palaeontologist Marta Oyelaran argues that the crest served for display to other members of the species rather than as an aerodynamic rudder for steering in flight.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Crest shape varies considerably from one species to another.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Crests are found only in adults, and are far larger in one sex than in the other.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Crested and uncrested pterosaur species occupied the same habitats.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The crest is built of dense bone and would have added little drag in flight.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ferrer's proposal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A shrub that grows on high Andean slopes fills its leaves with a bitter compound. Botanist Luis Ferrer proposes that the compound deters insect herbivores. A colleague argues instead that it screens the leaf against the intense ultraviolet light found at that altitude.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Leaves at the top of the shrub contain more of the compound than leaves lower down.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The compound is concentrated in the outermost cell layers of the leaf.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The compound absorbs strongly in the ultraviolet part of the spectrum.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Plants grown under insect-proof netting produce far less of the compound than exposed plants at the same altitude.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A coppiced hazel stool is cut back to the ground every seven years and throws up a fresh crop of straight poles from the surviving root, and it can be worked this way for centuries. Felling the same hazel outright yields considerably more wood at once, but the stool is then gone for good. A woodland manager who compared the two practices by the volume removed in a single year would therefore _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: underestimate the volume that a felled hazel yields.

choices.label: B
choices.content: overstate the long-run return from felling.

choices.label: C
choices.content: find coppicing the more productive of the two in that year.

choices.label: D
choices.content: conclude that a coppiced stool never regrows.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Giant tubeworms crowd around hydrothermal vents on the deep seafloor, far below any sunlight. An adult worm has neither mouth nor gut. What it has instead is a body cavity packed with bacteria that oxidise the hydrogen sulphide streaming out of the vent and build sugars from it. If the vent a colony sits on ceases to flow, the colony _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: can fall back on filtering particles from the surrounding water.

choices.label: B
choices.content: loses the chemical supply on which its food production depends.

choices.label: C
choices.content: migrates along the ridge to a vent that is still erupting.

choices.label: D
choices.content: reverts to obtaining its energy from sunlight.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Rubbish pits tell an excavator more than temples do, because nobody arranges them for posterity. The pit behind the fort's granary produced three things the archaeologists had not expected _____ a child's leather shoe, a wooden writing tablet and the better part of a barrel of oysters.

choices.label: C
choices.content: not expected, and a child's leather

choices.label: D
choices.content: not expected which are a child's leather

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: This is the only lock on the canal still worked entirely by hand, and the keeper lives in the cottage built beside it. He opened the upper paddles a little before dawn _____ the barge was through the lock and moored below the town by noon.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The flight had been sold as a gentle hour over the valley, and for most of it that is what it was. The balloon rose steadily for forty minutes _____ then the burner went out and the basket dropped nearly a hundred metres before the pilot could relight it.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Saturn's outermost ring is faint, enormously wide, and fed from a source outside the ring system altogether. Enceladus, a moon barely five hundred kilometres across _____ vents plumes of water vapour from fractures near its south pole, and a part of that vapour freezes into the ring.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The pottery closed in 1924, and because no catalogue of its output was ever printed, its wares are now identified by eye alone. Neither the glaze recipe nor the firing schedules _____ recorded anywhere in the workshop notebooks that survive.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Work on the wreck is done in pairs at a depth of forty metres, in water cold enough to limit a single dive to twenty minutes. The surface team monitors all four _____ air supply continuously, and any diver whose gauge falls below a set pressure is called up at once.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The bell tower at the corner of the square looks untouched from the piazza below, and the guidebooks still describe it as medieval. Having been rebuilt twice since the earthquake of 1908, the campanile _____ almost nothing of its original fabric above the foundations.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Resurfacing the ring road took an entire summer and cut the number of reported potholes by four fifths within a year of the work being finished. _____ complaints from drivers about the condition of the road rose over the same period.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Desalination plants along the Gulf coast now supply most of the region's drinking water. _____ the concentrated brine they return to the sea is denser than seawater and sinks, settling over the seabed and smothering the animals that live in the sediment.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Pollen survives in buried soil for millennia and identifies the plants that were in flower when the soil was sealed. Pollen taken from inside a Bronze Age burial mound comes almost entirely from meadowsweet and other plants that flower in high summer. _____ the burial was made somewhere between June and August.

questions.stem: The student wants to correct a common misunderstanding about the object. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The Bayeux Tapestry is nearly 70 metres long.
  • It is embroidered in wool on linen rather than woven on a loom.
  • It depicts the events leading to the Norman conquest of England in 1066.
  • Halley's Comet, seen in that year, appears among the figures in its border.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Halley's Comet appears among the figures embroidered in the border of the tapestry.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The Norman conquest of England, the subject of the work, took place in 1066.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The Bayeux Tapestry is nearly 70 metres long and depicts the events leading to 1066.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Though it is called a tapestry, the object is embroidered in wool on linen rather than woven, so the name is inaccurate.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain how the three crops support one another. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Maize, beans and squash are planted together in a single mound.
  • The maize stalk gives the bean vine something to climb.
  • Bacteria on the bean roots add nitrogen to the soil.
  • Broad squash leaves shade the ground and suppress weeds.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The broad leaves of the squash shade the ground around the mound.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Maize, beans and squash are all planted together in a single mound.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The maize gives the beans something to climb, the beans add nitrogen to the soil through their roots, and the squash leaves shade out the weeds.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Bacteria living on the roots of the bean plants add nitrogen to the soil.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain how chinampas stay productive without irrigation. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Chinampas are narrow plots built up from lake mud in the shallow water at Xochimilco.
  • Willows planted along their edges hold the plots together with their roots.
  • Canals run between the plots on every side.
  • The soil stays wet without irrigation, and a chinampa can be cropped several times a year.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Because canals run between the plots on every side, the soil stays wet without irrigation, and a chinampa can be cropped several times a year.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Willows planted along the edges of a chinampa hold the plot together with their roots.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Plots at Xochimilco can be cropped several times in a single year.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Chinampas are narrow plots built up from lake mud in the shallow water at Xochimilco.

questions.stem: A beekeeper bottles a harvest in two jar sizes: a small jar holds 250 grams of honey and a large jar holds 450 grams. She fills 4 more small jars than large jars and uses exactly 6,600 grams of honey. How many large jars did she fill?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A coastal ferry charges one fare for a car and a different fare for a bicycle. A crossing carrying 3 cars and 5 bicycles collected $97, and a crossing carrying 2 cars and 9 bicycles collected $93. What is the fare, in dollars, for one car?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A pillar candle is 30 centimetres tall when it is lit and burns down at a constant rate. Forty-five minutes after it is lit the candle is 26.4 centimetres tall. How many minutes after it is lit will the candle be 12 centimetres tall?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A hoist in a granary may lift a total mass of no more than 900 kilograms. The operator, whose mass is 78 kilograms, rides up with sacks of grain that each have a mass of 34 kilograms. What is the greatest number of sacks that can ride with the operator?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A climbing gym sets its monthly charge, in dollars, by the rule \(C=29+k(v-3)\), where v is the number of visits in the month and k is a constant. A member who visited 11 times was charged $69. How many dollars is a member charged for 20 visits in a month?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A harbour gauge records the water level falling at a constant rate on an outgoing tide. At 2:00 p.m. the level is 4.6 metres and at 5:00 p.m. it is 2.8 metres. If the level keeps falling at the same rate, how many hours after 5:00 p.m. will it reach 1.6 metres?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A potter's kiln heats at a constant rate. Its temperature is 18°C when firing begins and 453°C after 3 hours. The glaze on the pots matures at 1,033°C. How many hours after firing begins does the kiln reach that temperature?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A machinist writes the cost of finishing a batch of parts, in dollars, as \(\frac{6x^{2}+13x-5}{3x-1}\), where x is the number of parts and \(x>1\). Which expression is equivalent to the machinist's cost?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A stunt kite is released from a cliff, and its height above the beach, in metres, t seconds after release is modelled by \(h(t)=-0.5t^{2}+12t+3\). What is the greatest height above the beach, in metres, that this model predicts?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A photographer stacks identical grey filters in front of a lens. Each filter passes \(\frac{1}{3}\) of the light that reaches it, so a stack of x filters passes \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x}\) of the light reaching the first filter. One stack passes \(\frac{1}{243}\) of that light. How many filters are in the stack?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A drone crosses a canyon along a path modelled by \(y=x^{2}-14x+40\), where x is the horizontal distance in metres from the canyon's western rim and y is the height in metres relative to the rims. The drone is level with the rims at two horizontal positions. How many metres apart are those two positions?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A packaging engineer writes the surface area of a closed carton that has a square base of side s centimetres and a height of h centimetres as \(A=2s^{2}+4sh\) square centimetres. Which expression gives h in terms of A and s?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A jeweller models the mass of a hollow silver bead of outer radius x millimetres as \(m(x)=\frac{x^{3}}{4}-2\) grams. A bead made to this design has a mass of 14 grams. What is its outer radius, in millimetres?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A wildlife trust holds $2,500 in a fund that grows by 4% of its value each year, with no money added or withdrawn. To the nearest dollar, how much will the fund hold 3 years from now?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A newspaper press prints 1,250 sheets every 8 minutes. Working at that constant rate, how many minutes does the press take to print 21,875 sheets?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A rucksack is marked down 20% in a sale, and a loyalty card then takes a further 15% off the sale price. A shopper using the card pays $102. What was the price of the rucksack, in dollars, before the sale?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem:
The table gives the mass of paper, in kilograms, that a school collected for recycling in each of four weeks.
WeekMass collected (kg)
142
258
361
439
The school had set a four-week goal of 250 kilograms. By what percent did the collected mass fall short of that goal?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: The three angles of a triangular window pane measure \((2x+10)\)°, \((3x-5)\)° and \((x+7)\)°. What is the measure, in degrees, of the largest of the three angles?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A guy wire runs in a straight line from the top of a radio mast to a ground anchor, making an angle of 30° with the level ground. The anchor is 24 metres from the foot of the mast. What is the length of the wire, in metres?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A rectangular swimming pool is 12 metres long and 5 metres wide, with a uniform depth of 1.6 metres. A pump delivers water at a constant 4 cubic metres per minute. How many minutes does the pump take to fill the empty pool to the brim?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: In a survey of 240 randomly selected households in a lakeside town, 54 households reported owning a canoe. There are 8,000 households in the town. Based on this survey, what is the best estimate of the number of households in the town that own a canoe?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A rectangular playing field measures 105 metres by 88 metres. A gravel path runs in a straight line from one corner of the field to the opposite corner. How many metres long is the path?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A walking-tour guide collected $8 from every visitor on one tour and took in $192 altogether. How many visitors were on the tour?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A baker divides 3.6 kilograms of dough equally among 8 loaf tins. What mass of dough, in kilograms, goes into each tin?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A bike-share scheme charges $2 to unlock a bicycle plus $0.25 for each minute of the ride. Which equation gives the total charge C, in dollars, for a ride lasting m minutes?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A tap is opened on a full water butt, and \(v(t)=54-6t\) gives the volume of water remaining, in litres, t minutes after the tap is opened. How many litres remain 5 minutes after the tap is opened?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A goods lift may carry a total mass of no more than 600 kilograms. Which inequality gives all the possible values of the total mass m, in kilograms, that the lift may carry?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A rectangular vegetable bed has a perimeter of 26 metres and a length of 8 metres. What is its width, in metres?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A gardener's compost heap gains mass steadily, and \(M(d)=12+0.8d\) gives its mass in kilograms d days after the heap is started. In this model, what does the 0.8 represent?
questions.subject: MATH

choices.label: A
choices.content: The mass, in kilograms, of the heap on the day it is started.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The number of kilograms by which the mass of the heap increases each day.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The number of days it takes the heap to gain 1 kilogram.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The mass, in kilograms, of the heap after 12 days.

questions.stem: A triangular pennant has a base of x centimetres and a height of 6 centimetres. Which expression gives the area of the pennant, in square centimetres?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A tiler's cost for one row of a border is \(5(2p+3)\) dollars, where p is the number of patterned tiles in the row. Which expression is equivalent to the cost of one row?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A crochet pattern spirals outward, and \(S(r)=4r^{2}\) gives the number of stitches worked after r complete rounds. How many stitches have been worked after 5 rounds?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A technician's calibration chart converts an input x into a display reading r by the rule \(r=\sqrt{x+7}\). Which input produces a display reading of 5?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: When a drop of water lands in a still pond, the area covered by the spreading ripple is modelled by \(R(t)=t^{2}+3t\) square centimetres, where t is the number of seconds since the drop landed. What area does the model give 4 seconds after the drop lands?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: An archivist splits \(x^{8}\) scanned pages into \(x^{3}\) equally sized batches, where \(x>1\). Which expression gives the number of pages in each batch?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A single yeast cell divides so that the number of cells present after n rounds of division is \(h(n)=2^{n}\). How many cells are present after 6 rounds?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A joiner uses 3 litres of varnish to cover 12 square metres of decking. At that rate, how many litres of varnish are needed to cover 40 square metres of decking?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A cinema screen has 250 seats, and 40% of them were occupied at one showing. How many seats were occupied at that showing?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem:
The table gives the number of books borrowed from a library branch in each of three months.
MonthBooks borrowed
January340
February295
March412
How many books in total were borrowed from the branch over the three months?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: The masses, in grams, of five posted letters are 12, 15, 15, 20 and 28. What is the median of these masses, in grams?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A straight fence post is driven into level ground, and the two angles that the post makes with the ground on either side of it add to 180°. One of these angles measures 118°. What is the measure, in degrees, of the other angle?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A jeweller's gift box is a rectangular prism measuring 9 centimetres by 5 centimetres by 4 centimetres. How many cubic centimetres of packing foam are needed to fill the box completely?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A cylindrical soup tin has a base of area 28 square centimetres and a height of 5 centimetres. What is the volume of the tin, in cubic centimetres?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A loading ramp rises 5 metres vertically while running 12 metres horizontally. How many metres long is the sloping surface of the ramp?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A supplier prints the same delivery charge on an invoice in two ways: as \(\frac{2}{3}(6x-9)\) dollars and as \(4x+c\) dollars, where x is the number of pallets ordered and c is a constant. The two expressions give the same charge for every value of x. What is the value of c?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: An accountant values a machine by the linear model \(V(t)=c-vt\), where t is the number of years since purchase and c and v are positive constants. The machine is valued at $19,400 after 3 years and at $12,200 after 7 years. What was the purchase price of the machine, in dollars?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A charity stall sells wristbands for $4 each and mugs for $11 each, and it will sell exactly 200 items in total. The stall must take in at least $1,500. What is the least number of mugs the stall must sell?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A rectangular courtyard is 3 metres longer than it is wide and has an area of 154 square metres. A stone path 1 metre wide is laid all the way around the outside of the courtyard. What is the area of the path, in square metres?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A laboratory's two conversion steps are modelled by \(f(x)=x^{2}-4x\) and \(g(x)=x+3\), applied in that order so that the reading g produces is fed into f. Which expression is equivalent to \(f(g(x))\)?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: An engineer subtracts one flow rate from another and needs the result as a single quotient, for \(x>1\). Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{3}{x+2}-\frac{2}{x-1}\)?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A runner covers 12 kilometres on Saturday at a constant speed of x kilometres per hour, then covers 12 kilometres on Sunday at a constant speed of \(x+2\) kilometres per hour. The two runs take 5 hours in total. What is the value of x?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A materials scientist reduces the quantity \(\sqrt[3]{27x^{12}}\cdot x^{-2}\), where \(x>0\). Which expression is equivalent to that quantity?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A sealed radiator loses the same fraction of its coolant every hour, so the volume remaining is \(A(t)=A_{0}r^{t}\) litres after t hours, where \(A_{0}\) and r are constants. After 2 hours 72 litres remain, and after 4 hours 40.5 litres remain. What is the value of \(A_{0}\)?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: In the xy-plane, the line \(y=2x+c\) touches the curve \(y=x^{2}-6x+11\) at exactly one point, where c is a constant. What is the value of c?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A workshop records the same batch of components in two ways, as \(5x+2y=k\) and as \(15x+6y=48\), where x and y are the numbers of two kinds of component and k is a constant. Every pair \((x, y)\) that satisfies one equation also satisfies the other. What is the value of k?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A polling organisation surveyed 500 randomly selected adults in a city and reported a mean daily commute time of 27.4 minutes, with an associated margin of error of 1.8 minutes at the 95% confidence level. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
questions.subject: MATH

choices.label: A
choices.content: It is plausible that the mean daily commute time of all adults in the city is between 25.6 and 29.2 minutes.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Every adult in the city has a daily commute time between 25.6 and 29.2 minutes.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Exactly 95% of the adults surveyed have a daily commute time between 25.6 and 29.2 minutes.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The mean daily commute time of all adults in the city must be exactly 27.4 minutes.

questions.stem: A quality inspector weighs two batches of bearings. Batch A contains 30 bearings with a mean mass of 52 grams, and batch B contains 20 bearings with a mean mass of 62 grams. What is the mean mass, in grams, of all 50 bearings?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A foundry casts an alloy in which the ratio of the mass of copper to the mass of zinc is 3 to 5. The foundry has 84 kilograms of copper and 120 kilograms of zinc and no other source of either metal. What is the greatest mass of the alloy, in kilograms, that the foundry can cast?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem:
The table gives a bakery's revenue, in dollars, in each quarter of one year.
QuarterRevenue ($)
First18,400
Second21,160
Third19,800
Fourth24,150
Suppose revenue rises from the fourth quarter to the next quarter by the same percent as it rose from the first quarter to the second. What would the next quarter's revenue be, in dollars?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A roof truss is an isosceles triangle whose two equal sides each measure 25 centimetres and whose base measures 14 centimetres. A vertical strut runs from the apex of the truss and meets the base at a right angle. What is the length of the strut, in centimetres?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A solid metal cylinder of radius 3 centimetres and height 16 centimetres is melted down and recast, with no loss of metal, as a solid cone of radius 6 centimetres. What is the height of the cone, in centimetres?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A surveyor's plot of land is a right triangle whose two acute corner angles measure \(x\)° and \(y\)°. The surveyor's notes record that \(\sin x^{\circ}=\frac{20}{29}\). What is the value of \(\cos y^{\circ}\)?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: Volunteers at a food bank pack exactly 100 boxes. A standard box takes 4 minutes to pack and a family box takes 7 minutes, and the volunteers have at most 560 minutes of packing time. What is the greatest number of family boxes the volunteers can pack?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A courier's price for a delivery is a fixed booking fee plus a constant charge for each kilometre travelled. A 14-kilometre delivery costs $23.60 and a 22-kilometre delivery costs $32.40. What is the cost, in dollars, of a 35-kilometre delivery?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: In a quiz league a team gains 5 points for each correct answer and loses 2 points for each incorrect answer. One team attempted all 40 questions and finished with 137 points. How many questions did that team answer correctly?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A grain silo is built as a cylinder of radius 4 metres and height 10 metres, topped by a cone of radius 4 metres and height 3 metres. The total volume of the silo can be written as \(V\pi\) cubic metres. What is the value of V?
questions.subject: MATH
